clue.text: See 27
Like one with toes but no middle fingers, say

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the word toes keeps only its outer letters once its middle is dropped

explanation.surface: A creature that has toes but lacks middle fingers is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no middle' strips OE from toes, leaving TS. 'Like' is a verb here, the slang DIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingers are an example of digits, the word for any finger or toe.

clue.text: Public disgrace among kinsmen, one left out

parts.note: among means in

indicators.note: out signals that the letters for one and left are taken away from the kinsmen word

parts.note: one's kinsmen form a family
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone is publicly shamed among relatives, and one of them is left out of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' gives IN, not an insertion signal; 'out' drops one and left from the relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is notoriety, a state of public dishonour or disgrace.

clue.text: Those frozen, as single room without love is found

parts.note: single is one, the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the room word goes around the love letter

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
something that is found somewhere lies there

explanation.surface: Somebody frozen in a single room, without love, is discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: CELL goes round O to make CELOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice lollies are frozen treats on sticks, British for popsicles, so they are those frozen.

clue.text: Rope fibre is secured by sailor, then cut

indicators.note: secured by means held inside, so the word is goes within the shortened sailor
cut signals that the sailor word loses its final letter

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rope fibre is fastened by a seaman and then trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the sailor's last letter; 'secured by' means held inside. 'then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is the stiff plant fibre from an agave used for making rope and twine.

clue.text: Rugby player's given talk, which is painful

definitions.text: Rugby player's given talk, which is painful

parts.note: a lock is a second-row forward in rugby
to jaw is to talk at length

explanation.surface: A rugby forward has been lectured, and found it painful.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a definition: the condition makes the jaw lock painfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus, commonly called by this name, is a painful condition where the jaw muscles spasm shut.

clue.text: Lush getting in ultra drunk has planted kiss on top of you

indicators.note: has planted means the kiss pair is set down inside the scrambled letters
drunk suggests the letters of in and ultra reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue the kiss sits on top of the next piece, so it comes before it

parts.note: X is the conventional sign for a kiss

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A drunk getting into the ultra-lush stuff plants a kiss on your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles the letters into LURIANT; 'has planted' sets the kiss, sitting on top of U, inside that mix after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxuriant growth is rich and abundant, a synonym for lush vegetation.

clue.text: Banks consuming all your savings, for starters

indicators.note: for starters means take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Banks are swallowing up every penny you have saved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like financial institutions; it means sandbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Cays are low banks or reefs of sand or coral in the sea.

clue.text: Danger as wildcat strikes heading into July

indicators.note: into means the shortened cat goes inside the month's letters

parts.note: Jy is a dictionary abbreviation for July

indicators.note: strikes heading means the first letter of the cat word is struck off

parts.note: a leopard is a big wild cat

explanation.surface: There is danger in the air as unofficial walkouts begin in July.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes heading' beheads the cat, leaving EOPARD; 'into' puts that between the two letters of the month's short form. The surface's wildcat strikes are unofficial walkouts.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in jeopardy is to be in danger or at risk.

clue.text: Aircrew's frantic Geronimos, say?

indicators.note: frantic suggests the letters are thrown into wild disorder

parts.note: the possessive letter is used here as an S

explanation.surface: Airmen let out frenzied shouts as they jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantic' rearranges the letters of AIRCREWS, the possessive S included.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo is a shout made when leaping, as by paratroopers, so it exemplifies battle shouts.

clue.text: Foreman's right missed, proving a mistake

indicators.note: missed means the right letter is left out

parts.note: a gaffer is a foreman or boss

explanation.surface: The foreman's correct call went astray, which proved to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFFER without its R; 'proving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder, an embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: See 20
Pudding in book really hollow nonsense

indicators.note: in means the pudding sits inside the book word

parts.note: a tome is a large book
a fool is a fruit and cream pudding

indicators.note: hollow means the word really is emptied, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A pudding featured in a recipe book is really empty nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'hollow' do the work. A fool is a British dessert of fruit folded into cream, not a silly person here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomfoolery is silly behaviour, foolish nonsense.

clue.text: Hair may be fine

definitions.meaning: light-coloured or blond hair is described this way
fine weather or a fine decision can be described as just or pleasant

explanation.definitionFit: Blond hair is called fair, and fair also means fine, as of weather.

clue.text: Ruin go-cart, customised vehicle

indicators.note: customised suggests the letters are modified into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks a go-cart by over-modifying it into a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'customised' rearranges RUIN GOCART.
explanation.definitionFit: A touring car is a type of saloon car, as raced in touring car championships.

clue.text: Hollywood supporter drawing cross

parts.note: Hollywood is in Los Angeles, LA
a bra is a supporting undergarment
a doodle is an idle drawing

explanation.surface: A Hollywood fan is sketching a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an X or an angry mood; it means a crossbreed dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The labradoodle is a crossbreed of a Labrador and a poodle.

clue.text: Fastening, though going together

parts.note: though means but
colours that are toning go together well

explanation.surface: Fastening things even though they match.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttoning a coat is doing it up, fastening it.

clue.text: Men in bar requiring bottle

indicators.note: in means the men go inside the bar word

parts.note: to bar something is to stop it
a crew is a team of men

explanation.surface: Men in a pub needing a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'requiring' is a link. The pub-sounding bar is really a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwtop is a bottle or jar closed with a threaded cap.

clue.text: Males turning up with relations for sweets

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: rams are male sheep
family ties are relations

explanation.surface: Men appear with their relatives to buy sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses RAMS. These are a British brand of sugar-coated chocolate buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarties are a brand of candy-coated chocolate sweets.

clue.text: One describes what's going on plain spud, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: plain means common, and a spud is a potato, slang tater

explanation.surface: A sports broadcaster says something about an ordinary potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you COMMON TATER is spoken to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A commentator gives a running description of events as they happen.

clue.text: He might employ a spinner with passion, bagging Lancashire's opener

indicators.note: bagging means the passion word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: anger is a passion, a strong emotion

indicators.note: opener picks out the first letter of Lancashire

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler using spin keenly gets the Lancashire opening batsman out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bagging' puts L inside ANGER. The surface is cricket, a spinner bowling the Lancashire opener; the spinner is a fishing lure.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is a fisherman, who may use a spinner as a rotating lure.

clue.text: Sing this — then I'll be square!

definitions.text: Sing this — then I'll be square!

parts.words: Sing this — then I'll be square!
parts.note: a song title whose number is eight squared, so the age reached is a perfect square

explanation.walkthrough: A Beatles song about growing old; the number in its title is 8 times 8, a square number, and 'square' also means old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: The song looks ahead to a future birthday, and that age is a square number.

clue.text: Bring home master, take away leader

indicators.note: take away leader means the first letter of the master word is dropped

parts.note: to master a skill is to learn it

explanation.surface: A head teacher arrives home and removes the head of the school.
explanation.walkthrough: LEARN without its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring home a wage is to earn it.

clue.text: It's easy carrying on about smoker, getting a few words in the papers

definitions.text: a few words in the papers

indicators.note: carrying means the easy word holds the rest within it

parts.note: a cinch is something easy

indicators.note: about means on goes around the smoker word

parts.note: taken as written
a lum is a Scottish word for a chimney, which smokes

explanation.surface: It is simple to chatter on about a smoker and get a little piece published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the smoker in ON, making OLUMN; 'carrying' sets that inside the easy word after its first letter. LUM is a Scots chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: A column inch is a unit of newspaper space, one inch of a column of print.

clue.text: See 27
African nation enclosed by another?

parts.note: the name of one African country appears in full within the name of a second African country

explanation.walkthrough: Not geographically enclosed: its name sits inside the name SOMALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: This West African republic's name is spelt out inside Somalia's.

clue.text: Two times about to manipulate a girl? Not quite — he's taken one more!

indicators.note: about means the two time letters go around everything else

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so two times give two Ts
the second of the two time letters
to rig something is to manipulate it

indicators.note: not quite means the girl word loses its last letter

parts.note: a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A man twice tries to manipulate a girl, falls short, and has taken yet another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the two time letters round the rest; 'Not quite' leaves MIS. The definition is one more wife than a bigamist.
explanation.definitionFit: A trigamist has three spouses at once, taking one more than a bigamist does.

clue.text: Panamanian port: food channel

definitions.meaning: a port city at the Caribbean end of the Panama Canal
the large intestine, a channel through which food passes

explanation.definitionFit: Colón is a port in Panama, and the colon is the main part of the large intestine.

clue.text: Dead, having mishandled gun, his epitaph issued

indicators.note: having mishandled suggests the letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man dead after mishandling a gun has his epitaph released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having mishandled' rearranges GUN HIS EPITAPH ISSUED into the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone buried in the ground, so dead.

clue.text: Through such sound advice, primarily, murder solved

indicators.note: solved means the letters are worked out into a new order
primarily picks the first letter of advice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Through good advice, mainly, a murder case is cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solved' rearranges A with MURDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum is the membrane in the ear through which sound is received.
